title: add-jsonschema-strict-mode-openai-compat-improved-errors
author: Ava Patel
description: Add JSON Schema-based structured output support (response_format="json_schema") with a strict validation mode and improved, OpenAI-compatible error reporting. Motivation: customers rely on structured responses for downstream parsing and strict validation is required for production workflows (e.g. payments, audit logs). This PR: 1) introduces response_format="json_schema" on the Redwood API OpenAI-compat layer, 2) implements server-side schema validation with a configurable "strict" flag that rejects responses which do not conform to the provided schema, 3) improves error messages to match OpenAI-compatible error structure and provide field-level diagnostics, 4) surfaces validation failures in streaming responses (graceful abort + final error object), 5) adds end-to-end tests and docs for the new behavior. Checklist: - [x] API contract and docs updates (redwood-docs) - [x] Runtime schema validator (fast-jsonschema-based) - [x] Streaming error protocol + client hints - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping for error codes and messages - [x] Backwards-compatible default (strict=false) Implementation notes: - New top-level request param response_format: "json_schema" accepted on create/completions/chat endpoints when using the OpenAI-compat path. - request param strict_mode (boolean) controls validation behavior: when "true" the runtime returns an HTTP 400/validation_error (OpenAI-compatible) and emits a structured error payload; when "false" the model output is returned but a "validation_warnings" header and runtime metric are emitted. - Streaming: on partial streaming, if a schema violation is detected the stream is terminated with a final JSON error frame matching OpenAI error fields (type, message, param, code) and a small human-friendly hint. - Error messages: field-level path, expected type, and offending token are included; errors map to standardized codes (e.g. invalid_schema, missing_required, extra_properties) to help clients implement retry/fallback logic. - Performance: validator runs incrementally during streaming to avoid large memory spikes; fallback path avoids full reserialization for common cases. Related: references earlier PRs adding structured output support and strict modes (pr-110234, pr-114512) and issues about streaming compatibility. Deployment notes: default for hosted API remains strict_mode=false; enterprise customers can opt in via per-route config; Dedicated/Private runtimes will include a rollout flag to toggle the validator. See release notes below for upgrade and compatibility guidance.

release_notes: Add response_format="json_schema" and strict_mode for structured output. Defaults to strict_mode=false to preserve existing behavior. Enabling strict_mode will cause invalid outputs to return a validation_error (OpenAI-compatible) and may change HTTP response codes for some requests; see docs for migration steps.
notes: Enterprise/Dedicated need to enable validator feature flag before enabling strict_mode in production
Monitoring: new validation.* metrics and events emitted to observability console
example_error_payload: {"error":{"type":"invalid_schema","message":"Response failed JSON Schema validation: missing required property 'amount'","param":"response","code":"validation_error"}}
examples: Behavior: HTTP 400 + OpenAI-compatible error body when model output does not match schema
Streaming: final error frame with OpenAI-compatible error structure and abort
testing: unit: validator edge cases (type mismatches, required fields, additionalProperties)
integration: streaming abort + final error frame verification
e2e: SDKs parse final error frame and raise client error
backport_plan: No backport to older releases by default. Critical fixes only; see changelog and internal rollout doc for backport decisions.
security_considerations: Validator executes on model outputs only and uses sandboxed JS-based schema engine; size limits and execution timeouts enforced to avoid DoS.
user_impact: Opt-in feature. When enabled with strict_mode=true clients may observe validation_error responses; clients should handle OpenAI-compatible error codes and optionally fallback to non-strict path.
